title: Microsoft offers to buy out a quarter of its workforce
summary: Employees in the US, Canada, India, and the UK may receive offers to leave MS today.
body: On Monday, Microsoft said it will offer voluntary buyouts to eligible employees in select parts of the company. CNBC reports that the buyouts will be offered to roughly 60,000 employees , or about a quarter of its global workforce. The company describes the offer as an opportunity for employees who may have already been considering career moves outside Microsoft. While Microsoft did not give a direct reason for the buyout package, it comes as the company has spent the last several years managing costs amid investment in AI infrastructure and data-center buildout. Microsoft will extend the voluntary exit offer (VEO) to qualifying employees in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Microsoft employees at level 70 or below will be eligible for the buyout program. The company's employee rankings are internal, but according to the salary and career database Levels.fyi , levels 65–67 correspond to principal positions, and 68–70 are at the partner/distinguished level. According to Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, eligible organizations were selected "based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs." title: الكرة الذهبية.. أوناي سميون أفضل حارس في العالم
summary: مرمى إسبانيا في أمان
body: مرمى إسبانيا في أمان حصد أوناي سميون، حارس أتلتيك بيلباو ومنتخب إسبانيا ، جائزة أفضل حارس في العالم خلال حفل الكرة الذهبية الذي أقيم، اليوم الاثنين، في العاصمة الإنجليزية لندن. وتنافس سميون على الجائزة مع 9 حراس بارزين، هم ياسين بونو (المغرب - الهلال) - تيبو كورتوا (بلجيكا - ريال مدريد) - خوان جارسيا (إسبانيا - برشلونة) - جريجور كوبيل (سويسرا - دورتموند) - إيمليانو مارتينيز (الأرجنتين - تشيلسي) - إدواردو ميندي (السنغال - الأهلي) - ديفيد رايا (إسبانيا - آرسنال) - ماتفي سافونوف (روسيا - باريس سان جيرمان) - أوناي سيمون - فوزينيا (كاب فيردي - كولو كولو). ويُعد التتويج بكأس العالم 2026 العامل الأبرز وراء حصد سميون للجائزة، بعدما كان الحارس الأساسي للماتادور أثناء المونديال. وحصل سميون على جائزة القفاز الذهبي كأفضل حارس في البطولة، بعدما استقبل هدفا واحدا خلال 8 مباريات. ولم يكتف حارس أتلتيك بيلباو برفع الكأس، بل سجل أيضًا أطول سلسلة في تاريخ البطولة دون استقبال أي هدف، بعدما حافظ على نظافة شباكه لمدة 650 دقيقة متتالية، امتدت من آخر مباراتين له في كأس العالم 2022 إلى أول 6 مباريات ونصف في نسخة 2026. ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة

title: Worms mate in man's eyes, get plucked out right before larvae burst out
summary: Case study gives a whole new meaning to "bedroom eyes."
body: After two months of discomfort, a man in South Korea went to an eye clinic where doctors pulled 11 living, wriggling worms from his eyes. They apparently made the most of their time on the man's peepers; at the time of extraction, many of the female worms were pregnant. The man narrowly avoided having them spew their loads of living larvae directly into his eyes. The man in this case was a 71-year-old crop farmer. He told doctors that for the previous two months he had the sensation of having something stuck in both his eyes, which were also red and blurry. When ophthalmologists took a look, they quickly saw the problem: multiple mobile, whitish roundworms. His eyes were not in good shape either, as one might expect. The blood vessels in the membrane over the eye, the conjunctiva, were enlarged, making his eyes look red. And the cells of his cornea—the transparent, dome-shaped outer layer of the eye—had eroded, potentially after the helminths' hanky-panky. According to a case report published in the New England Journal of Medicine , the doctors gave the man a topical treatment to numb his eyes and then began plucking out the worms one by one with fine forceps. body: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle created one of the most beloved fictional detectives of all time in Sherlock Holmes, spawning countless novels, films, TV series, and so forth featuring the sleuth. title: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo
summary: Investigators explain how highway thieves stole $100M in data center equipment.
body: Highway thieves are using sophisticated digital tactics that investigators worry make it easy to rob trucks carrying millions in expensive data center equipment. NBC News spoke to “several industry leaders, consultants, and investigators advising law enforcement” offices probing the biggest thefts yet and reported that since June, thieves have “made away with more than $100 million in data center freight.” Here’s how they said thieves get away with it: First, thieves hack freight brokers’ accounts on shipment-listing websites and post fake shipments to lure real bids, then send a malicious link to any trucking companies that respond. Once victims click, thieves install software to take control of their accounts and start bidding on real shipments. Sometimes, a real delivery driver is hired to collect the cargo, unaware of the scam, and other times fake driver’s licenses are used to get accomplices hired. Either way, the goods are eventually transferred to a driver working with the thieves to resell the gear, and, in one of the largest thefts, tracking coordinates were spoofed to prevent digital monitoring. The Internet is currently overflowing with images of busted iPhone Duos, all sporting almost identical damage. The OLED is marred by several bright lines originating just below the midpoint of the display. These bands of damaged pixels extend all the way to the bottom and right edges. Some units also show lines of dead pixels following the crease from the top to the area where the bright lines begin. Anyone who has seen a damaged OLED panel will be familiar with this type of defect. When the layers of the display are damaged, the pixels no longer receive the correct voltage to illuminate them. title: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
summary: A new model suggests Mars may host ice-forming physics never directly observed before.
body: Every morning during the Martian spring and summer, a thin and extremely long cloud emerges, only to disappear again. The wispy formation appears near the volcano Arsia Mons and gradually elongates until it reaches over 1,000 miles—about the distance from New York to Kansas City as the crow flies—before dissipating. This cycle then repeats for several months. Since it was first recorded by a probe in 2018, scientists have been unable to find a plausible explanation for the existence of this cloud, often referred to as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC). Until now. title: Ice sheet expansion may have started 2,000 years ago, but we canceled that
summary: The tiny remains of the Laurentide Ice Sheet began getting somewhat less tiny.
body: Barnes Ice Cap sits on the central plateau of Baffin Island, in the Canadian Arctic. It is the last surviving fragment of the Laurentide Ice Sheet, the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, which at its peak buried most of Canada under two miles of ice and locked away around 80 meters of sea level. That remnant has now yielded direct physical evidence that ice sheets might have reversed their retreat and started to grow again thousands of years ago. In a recent Science study, researchers show that the Laurentide reached its smallest size about 3,600 years ago, then started re-expanding roughly 2,000 years ago, which the team interprets as the opening move of the next glaciation. Apparently, this brand-new ice age was on its way until about 1960, when human-caused climate warming reversed it. title: Crows can evaluate visual info twice as fast as mammals
summary: Birds' compact nervous system seems to help them handle tasks very quickly.
body: Much of what we know about how a brain makes decisions comes from studying monkeys watching dots. In a task known as a random-dot-motion task, a cloud of flickering specks drifts weakly in one direction while the subject tries to determine whether—and in which direction— it’s moving. The task has shown that in the primate neocortex, neurons gather visual evidence over time, with their firing rates climbing until they cross a threshold, when the animal commits to a decision.
